d6dbf25272: Why is −7 mod 3 equal to 2, not −1?

7cef54fa8f: By fast (binary) exponentiation: repeatedly squaring a mod n and multiplying in the factors corresponding to the binary digits of b, taking the modulus at every step. This needs only about log₂(b) multiplications, so even a 1000-digit exponent computes instantly.
6ab8d023a5: What is the modulo operation used for?
595ddb187d: Clock and calendar arithmetic, hash tables, checksums, cryptography (RSA relies on modular exponentiation), pseudo-random number generators, and cycling through array indices.

7b10bfecb0: How is congruence different from equality?
7a8f480029: Equality means two numbers are identical. Congruence mod n is weaker: it only requires them to leave the same remainder when divided by n, so infinitely many numbers (…, b−n, b, b+n, b+2n, …) are all congruent to b.

c2322c875a: Each hex digit represents exactly 4 binary bits, so a byte is always exactly 2 hex digits — a much more compact and readable way to write binary data, used for memory addresses, color codes and more.

9af1b46783: Both are shorthand for binary: octal (base 8) groups bits in 3s, hexadecimal (base 16) groups them in 4s. Hex is more common today because it aligns with 8-bit bytes; octal remains in use for Unix file permissions.
